Basically, it's information that outlets are asked not to release until a certain date and time. The science community releases studies and news to various outlets with an embargo set. If the outlet breaks the embargo, i.e. publishes the content early, they will be barred from receiving content from that source, and possibly others, in the future. In the context of r/Science, they're attempting to get on the science community's good side by following embargo rules in an effort to become a major science news outlet in the future.

This sort of embargo shit is rife in the gaming industry as far as reviews are concerned. Similarly to above, a publisher will place an embargo on reviews for games until AFTER the game has released so that bad reviews do not harm initial sales (often when sales are the strongest). If an outlet breaks the embargo, they will not receive reviews copies from that publisher in the future, which can and will have a major negative impact on the viability of said outlet. An extremely shady practice.
